policy: Only facts with a written basis are recorded here. Everything else stays 'unknown' in the normalized reference model. Do not add values that have not been checked against the cited basis.

notes: Name as printed: Scatophaga stercoraria. Family in the source: Muscidae: Helomyzides.
Family assignment: Scatophaga is an older spelling of Scathophaga, the type genus of Scathophagidae; S. stercoraria is the yellow dung fly.
Plate caption: 'Fig. 3 a, head of Scatophaga stercoraria; 3 b, antenna; 3 c, wing.'

The engraving is small (about 360 px wide in the 300 dpi scan); the plate shows the wing tilted with its base on the right, so the crop was mirrored and rotated 24.5° to put the base on the left and the costa on top.
A tuft of hairs near the base and the doubled engraving lines at the base appear as short extra pieces.
Tracing quality: fair. Automatic centre-line tracing; compare with the scan in Vein review before using details.

notes: Name as printed: Sarcophaga mortuorum. Family in the source: Muscidae: Sarcophagides.

Family assignment: Walker's Sarcophaga mortuorum is Linnaeus' Musca mortuorum (he cites 'mortuorum, L. 1761'), now Cynomya mortuorum, a blow fly (Calliphoridae) — not a flesh fly, despite the genus name used in 1853.
Plate caption: 'Fig. 4. Sarcophaga mortuorum, male. 4 a, extremity of abdomen, sideways'.
Whole-fly drawing: the wing base is hidden by the thorax and was cut off at about 20% of the wing length; nothing was traced there.
Legs, antennae or bristles cross the wing in the engraving; short pieces near them may belong to them, not to veins.
The plate shows the wing with its base on the right; the crop was mirrored.
Tracing quality: rough. Automatic centre-line tracing; compare with the scan in Vein review before using details.
calliphoridae-walker-mortuorum.basis: Figure number, name and family heading transcribed from the printed caption (Walker 1853, scan leaf n314); orientation set during tracing; the figure carries no scale bar.
